Feature importance: observed-upper u/v model

Model conus-depth1to10-upperuv-20261009-01, using only its 12,107 selected trees. This is the same model used by the profile tabs. Both training VID thresholds are 6.6.

96 inputs: 29 density slots + 29 u slots + 29 v slots + nine height, time, location and upper-VID inputs. Slots start at the observed edge; hidden lower layers are excluded. Only density slots are normalized and cube-root transformed. Velocities remain in m/s.

Training gain

Total gain sums improvements in the training objective attributed to splits on a feature. It is neither explained variance nor the improvement that removing a feature would cause. Correlated features can substitute for each other. The Model performance tab provides the paired retraining comparison with and without u/v.

Contributions to held-out predictions

Exact TreeSHAP on 21 profiles / 105 rows: one fixed profile per held-out radar from the existing random 2025 gallery, with five target depths each. Selection does not use prediction errors. These profiles illustrate behavior; this small sample does not estimate population importance or causal biological effects.

Values are contributions to cube-root normalized density, not birds/km³. Contributions plus the baseline reproduce that model output; maximum reconstruction error: 2.1e-05. To recover density, sum contributions first, cube and clip, then multiply by upper VID. Individual SHAP values cannot be cubed separately.

Group totals sum absolute contributions, so they depend on group size and correlated inputs; the feature count is shown in parentheses. Velocity availability may carry measurement-quality cues as well as movement information.

Reproduction

Run python analysis/depth-diagnostics/attribute-upperuv.py, then render this RMarkdown. Attribution uses Python XGBoost; all figures are generated in R. The audit, gain, SHAP and row-level contributions are stored alongside this report. Earlier location/AGL model diagnostics are archived under pre-upperuv/ and their original CSVs; they are not mixed with the current-model attribution.
